justification: The bias-free field anomaly repeats on the same section (mean r 0.706, 35/38 pairs beat phase surrogates at p < 0.05; different-section null mean 0.365). Driving proxies explain a median 47% of it (the train's own traction field), but the residual still repeats (mean r 0.499, 31/38 significant, null mean 0.22, p95 0.408), also in the mid-section away from the pull-away traction peak (mean r 0.549, 24/38 significant, null p95 0.523). So there is a position-locked component, modest and not yet separable from non-linear traction effects that repeat because drivers run each section alike. Use it as a low-weight DTW feature; the ablation decides. |B| itself stays NO-GO.
